gui.app.title: osu! Tablet Assistant
gui.baseline.intro: Before changing anything we take two quick measurements with your current settings, so we can tell whether a new setting is really better. Make sure OpenTabletDriver is running and your pen moves the cursor. Each test takes a few seconds.
gui.baseline.skip_note: You can skip these tests, but the suggestions will then be more generic.
gui.baseline.title: Your starting point
gui.close.restore_question: A test option is still active in OpenTabletDriver. Restore the settings you had before? ("No" leaves it as it is.)
gui.close.title: Close the assistant
gui.details.title: Technical details
gui.detect.failed_hint: Tip: start OpenTabletDriver once with your tablet plugged in, or choose its folders by hand.
gui.detect.intro: We look for OpenTabletDriver on this computer and read your current settings. Make sure it is installed and that your tablet has been connected at least once.
gui.detect.safe_note: This step only reads files. Nothing is changed.
gui.detect.title: Find OpenTabletDriver
gui.display.detect_failed: The screen could not be detected. Please type its values.
gui.display.intro: The tablet area is mapped onto your screen, so we need the size of the monitor you play osu! on.
gui.display.invalid: Please enter valid numbers (size and refresh rate must be above zero).
gui.display.left_help: Where the left edge of that monitor is on your desktop. 0 for your main monitor.
gui.display.multi_monitor: Several monitors? Detection only finds your main one. If you play on another monitor, type its size and its left/top position as shown in Windows display settings (for example 1920 if it sits to the right of a 1920-pixel-wide main monitor).
gui.display.refresh_help: Shown in Windows display settings, for example 60, 144 or 240.
gui.display.title: Your screen
gui.display.top_help: Where the top edge is. Usually 0.
gui.display.width_help: Horizontal resolution of the monitor you play on.
gui.questions.intro: These answers help choose sensible starting settings. Nothing here is permanent.
gui.questions.keep_area.label: Keep my current area width ({width} mm)
gui.questions.keep_area.title: Keep your current area size?
gui.questions.keep_area.why: Why we ask: if you already like how big your area feels, we keep its width and only adjust the rest.
gui.questions.map_preference.title: What kind of maps do you play most?
gui.questions.map_preference.why: Why we ask: jump maps reward precise long moves; stream maps need a very steady cursor.
gui.questions.notices_input_lag.label: Yes, the cursor feels like it lags behind my hand
gui.questions.notices_input_lag.title: Do you feel input lag?
gui.questions.notices_input_lag.why: Why we ask: if the cursor feels late, we avoid options that add delay.
gui.questions.notices_jitter.label: Yes, I see the cursor shaking when I hold the pen still
gui.questions.notices_jitter.title: Does your cursor shake?
gui.questions.notices_jitter.why: Why we ask: if you see tremor while holding the pen still, we give noise reduction more weight.
gui.questions.play_style.title: How do you move the pen?
gui.questions.play_style.why: Why we ask: big arm movements need a larger tablet area; finger and wrist aiming work better with a smaller one.
gui.questions.priority.title: What matters more to you?
gui.questions.priority.why: Why we ask: filters can make the cursor smoother, but most of them add a tiny delay.
gui.questions.skill_level.title: How experienced are you?
gui.questions.skill_level.why: Why we ask: beginners usually benefit from more smoothing; experienced players tend to prefer raw, direct input.
gui.questions.title: About you
gui.result.apply_confirm: Apply these settings to OpenTabletDriver now? Your original settings are backed up first ({backup}).
gui.result.dry_run_note: Dry-run mode: nothing is applied. Load the saved preset from OpenTabletDriver's Presets menu when you want to use it.
gui.result.nothing: No option has been chosen yet. Go back and test or choose one.
gui.result.preset_confirm: Save these settings as a preset in OpenTabletDriver's Presets folder? A backup is made first. Nothing is applied.
gui.result.title: Your result
gui.tablet.approx_note: Sizes come from OpenTabletDriver's tablet definitions. The report rate is the manufacturer's nominal value and may be approximate; you can correct any value with the form below.
gui.tablet.col.name: Tablet
gui.tablet.custom.invalid: Please enter a name and positive numbers.
gui.tablet.custom.name: Name
gui.tablet.custom_help: Use the active area from your tablet's specifications (not the outer size). Report rate is how many positions per second it sends; 133 is typical for entry-level tablets.
gui.tablet.custom_title: My tablet is not in the list
gui.tablet.intro: Pick your tablet from the list. Tablets already set up in OpenTabletDriver come first. If yours is not listed, type its size below.
gui.tablet.no_profiles_at_all: OpenTabletDriver has no tablet profile yet. Connect your tablet, start OpenTabletDriver so it creates one, then go back one step and search again.
gui.tablet.pick_profile: This tablet has no OpenTabletDriver profile with the same name. Choose which profile to use:
gui.tablet.profile_linked: Its OpenTabletDriver profile was found; changes will go there.
gui.tablet.selected: Selected: {name} - {w} x {h} mm, up to {rate} reports per second.
gui.tablet.title: Your tablet
gui.tablet.unknown_profile: OpenTabletDriver knows this tablet, but we do not have its size. Please fill in the form below.
gui.test.aim.desc: Click a series of circles. Measures accuracy and speed.
gui.test.aim.name: Aim test
gui.test.rate.desc: Measures how many positions per second reach the cursor. A low number can point to a limited tablet or a driver problem.
gui.test.rate.name: Report rate test
gui.test.stillness.desc: Measures how much the cursor trembles while the pen is still.
gui.test.stillness.name: Stability test
gui.test.tracking.desc: Follow a moving dot. Measures delay, accuracy and smoothness.
gui.test.tracking.name: Tracking test
gui.testing.consent: To test options, this assistant applies them to OpenTabletDriver one by one. Your current settings are backed up first ({backup}) and you can restore them at any time. Continue?
gui.testing.consent_backup_new: a backup will be made now
gui.testing.cancelled: Test cancelled. Finished tests are kept; press "Apply and test" to measure this option again.
gui.testing.finished: Done. You can rate it, test another option or refine.
gui.testing.intro: These are settings that could suit you. Pick one and press "Apply and test": we apply it to OpenTabletDriver, you do three short tests, and we score it. Try as many as you like, rate how they feel, and ask for a refinement of the best one whenever you want.
gui.testing.intro_dry: Dry-run mode: nothing is applied or measured. Read the options and pick the one you want to export.
gui.testing.rating_help: 1 = bad, 5 = great. Your feeling counts in the score.
gui.testing.refined: A refined option was added to the list.
gui.testing.restore_confirm: Put back the settings you had when you started?
gui.testing.title: Try settings
gui.welcome.disclaimer: This assistant gives measured, explainable starting points, not a guaranteed perfect setting: every hand and every tablet is different, and you can keep fine-tuning afterwards. Before it changes anything it always makes a backup of your OpenTabletDriver settings, and it only applies something when you confirm.
gui.welcome.dry_run: Dry-run mode is on: nothing will be applied to OpenTabletDriver. You will only get a preset file and a report.
gui.welcome.intro: This assistant helps you set up OpenTabletDriver for osu!. It looks at your tablet, asks a few questions, tries some settings while you draw and click, and suggests the tablet area and filters that work best for you.
gui.welcome.title: Welcome
gui.welcome.what_happens:
What will happen:
1. We find OpenTabletDriver and your tablet.
2. You tell us how you play.
3. You do a few short pen tests (a few seconds each).
4. We try some settings, measure them and suggest the best one.
5. You decide whether to save it or apply it.
